chunks: Thus, We never sent an admonisher to a settlement before you but the decadent among them said, 'We found our fathers following this way, and we are walking in their footsteps.'
ai.seo_question: What was the common excuse of the wealthy leaders when prophets came to them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the intellectual stagnation of the 'mutrafūn' (the affluent elite) who equated ancestral tradition with truth, thereby rejecting the necessity of independent reasoning (ijtihad) in the face of prophetic revelation. It serves as a critique of taqlid (blind imitation) when it becomes an end in itself rather than a means to truth, a concept central to Usuli jurisprudence. The verse underscores that divine guidance requires active acceptance, not merely passive adherence to the customs of the past.
